# Contract: Frontend Shell and Dashboard

*Generated by spec-writer. Hand edits are overwritten on regeneration.*

## Prerequisites

These conditions describe the environment in which items in this
contract are exercised. Producing them is part of the feature's
deliverable, alongside the implementation itself — a contract whose
prerequisites are not yet satisfied is not failing, it is still being
built. Once the feature is delivered, any missing condition halts item
execution until it is restored.

**Runtime services:**
- Node.js 24 (any version satisfying the `engines` range of the frontend project, 22.12 or newer) and `npm` are on PATH; frontend dependencies are installed with `npm ci` in `frontend/`
- a Chromium browser is available to a browser driver for UI and E2E items (installed with the browser driver's install command)
- a stand-in for the BugFlow API is running on a loopback port it reports when it starts (default 8100); it serves the F09 endpoints that the frontend calls under `/api/v1`, answers CORS for the origin `http://localhost:3000`, and exposes a control interface (switch scenario, read the record of received requests, reset); it is delivered by this feature under `frontend/tests/mocks/` and is started with `npm run mock:api` in `frontend/`
- the frontend development server is running on port 3000 (`npm run dev` in `frontend/`), with `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` pointing at the stand-in for Service, CLI and UI items, or at the real API for E2E items
- for E2E items only: Docker Engine with Compose v2 is running and the `db` service of `docker-compose.yml` is healthy; `uv` is on PATH and backend dependencies are installed with `uv sync` in `backend/`; the real BugFlow API (F09) is running on `127.0.0.1:8000` with default CORS (`http://localhost:3000`) and can be stopped and started again during an item; no real LLM key is needed because no E2E item calls the LLM

**Persistent state:**
- `empty-database`: the real database has its schema initialized and holds no rows in any application table. Used by `E2E-DASHBOARD-02`, `E2E-DASHBOARD-04`.
- `seeded-database`: the real database has its schema initialized and holds the 20 packaged sample bugs, all with status `open`, and exactly one run of type `seed` with status `succeeded` and progress 20 of 20; no result rows and no embeddings exist. Used by `E2E-DASHBOARD-01`, `E2E-DASHBOARD-03`, `E2E-ENUM-LABELS-01`.

**Static inputs:**
- `frontend/tests/fixtures/enums.json` — the body of `GET /meta/enums` with all 11 canonical enums (`BugStatus`, `Environment`, `Team`, `Component`, `Severity`, `ResolutionStatus`, `Priority`, `Seniority`, `RunType`, `RunStatus`, `StepStatus`), each value with `code`, `label` and `definition`, equal in codes and labels to the backend enum module (for example `Component` includes `ui_ux` labelled "UI/UX" and `ResolutionStatus` includes `wont_fix` labelled "Won't fix"). Used by: `SVC-ENUM-PROVIDER-01`, `SVC-ENUM-PROVIDER-02`, `SVC-ENUM-PROVIDER-03`, `UI-DASHBOARD-CONTENT-02`, `UI-DASHBOARD-CONTENT-03`, `UI-DASHBOARD-CONTENT-04`, `CLI-ENUM-SOURCE-01`, `CLI-ENUM-SOURCE-02`.
- `frontend/tests/fixtures/enums-custom-labels.json` — the same shape as `enums.json` with three changed labels: `BugStatus` `open` is "Awaiting triage", `RunType` `triage` is "Agent triage" and `Component` `ui_ux` is "Interface and UX". Used by: `UI-ENUM-LABELS-01`.
- `frontend/tests/fixtures/stats-populated.json` — the body of `GET /stats` with `total` 20, `by_status` open 17, processing 1, processed 2, failed 0, `by_component` with `frontend` 1, `backend` 1 and every other component 0, `by_severity` with critical 0, major 1, minor 1. Used by: `SVC-API-CLIENT-03`, `UI-DASHBOARD-CONTENT-01`, `UI-DASHBOARD-CONTENT-02`, `UI-DASHBOARD-CONTENT-03`, `UI-DASHBOARD-CONTENT-04`, `UI-DASHBOARD-CONTENT-08`.
- `frontend/tests/fixtures/stats-empty.json` — the body of `GET /stats` with `total` 0 and every count in `by_status`, `by_component` and `by_severity` 0. Used by: `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-02`, `UI-DASHBOARD-CONTENT-08`.
- `frontend/tests/fixtures/runs-recent.json` — the body of `GET /runs` as `{items}` with 12 runs, newest first, ids 21 down to 10: run 21 has type `triage` and status `running` with no finish time; run 20 has type `index`, status `succeeded`, started 2026-10-12T10:00:00Z and finished 2026-10-12T10:01:02Z; run 19 has type `triage`, status `succeeded`, started 2026-10-12T09:00:00Z and finished 2026-10-12T09:00:41Z; run 18 has type `seed`, status `failed`, started and finished 12 seconds apart; run 17 has type `reset` and status `queued` with no finish time; runs 16 to 10 are `succeeded` runs of mixed types with finish times. Used by: `UI-DASHBOARD-CONTENT-05`, `UI-DASHBOARD-CONTENT-06`, `UI-DASHBOARD-CONTENT-07`, `UI-RESPONSIVE-LAYOUT-04`, `SVC-API-CLIENT-05`.
- `frontend/tests/fixtures/run-7-finished.json` — the body of `GET /runs/7` as `{run, steps, logs}`: run 7 of type `triage`, bug 1, status `succeeded`, progress 5 of 5; five steps with positions 1 to 5 and keys `component_classifier`, `severity_classifier`, `technical_analyst`, `resolution_manager`, `bug_documenter`, all `succeeded` with input, output and duration; four log lines. The stand-in also serves the same data as an event stream (step, log and run events, then close). Used by: `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-01`.
- `frontend/tests/fixtures/run-8-live-script.json` — a script the stand-in plays for run 8 (type `triage`): step 1 becomes `running` at 0 ms and `succeeded` at 400 ms, steps 2 to 5 follow at 400 ms intervals, a log line accompanies each transition, and the run becomes `succeeded` at 2,000 ms; the same timeline backs `GET /runs/8` at any moment. Used by: `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-02`, `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-03`, `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-04`, `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-05`, `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-06`.

**Configuration:**
- by default `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` is `http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/v1` (the stand-in) and the stand-in scenario is `populated`: it serves `enums.json`, `stats-populated.json`, `runs-recent.json` (honouring the `limit` query parameter), run 7 and run 8, and an error envelope with status 404 for any other run or bug id; it accepts the write endpoints and answers them in the F09 shapes (201 with a bug for create, 200 for edit, reopen, init and reset, 202 with `run_ids` for seed, index and triage). Applies to every Service, CLI and UI item unless a line below overrides it.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` unset: the frontend uses `http://localhost:8000/api/v1`. Used by `SVC-API-CLIENT-02`.
- `trailing-slash`: `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` ends with a slash. Used by `SVC-API-CLIENT-01`.
- scenario `empty`: as `populated`, but `GET /stats` answers `stats-empty.json` and `GET /runs` answers `{items: []}`. Used by `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-02`.
- scenario `slow`: as `populated`, but every reply is delayed by 1,500 ms. Used by `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-01`.
- scenario `unavailable`: every endpoint except the control interface answers status 503 with the envelope `{"error": {"code": "service_unavailable", "message": "Database is unavailable", "details": []}}`. Used by `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-06`.
- scenario `enums-unavailable`: as `populated`, but only `GET /meta/enums` answers the `unavailable` envelope. Used by `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-07`, `SVC-ENUM-PROVIDER-04`.
- scenario `runs-error`: as `populated`, but only `GET /runs` answers status 500 with the envelope message "Internal server error". Used by `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-08`.
- scenario `custom-labels`: as `populated`, but `GET /meta/enums` answers `enums-custom-labels.json`. Used by `UI-ENUM-LABELS-01`.
- scenario `stats-changes`: as `populated`, and the stand-in can be told to switch to `empty` data without restarting. Used by `UI-DASHBOARD-CONTENT-08`.
- `validation-error`: as the default, but `POST /bugs` answers status 422 with the envelope code `validation_error` and details `[{"field": "title", "message": "must be at most 120 characters"}]`. Used by `SVC-API-CLIENT-10`.
- `bad-gateway`: as the default, but `GET /stats` answers status 502 with a plain-text body. Used by `SVC-API-CLIENT-12`.
- scenario `no-sse`: as `populated`, but `GET /runs/{id}/events` answers status 404 for every run. Used by `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-03`, `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-04`.
- scenario `sse-drop`: as `populated`, but the event stream of run 8 is closed by the stand-in after two events, before the run is terminal, while `GET /runs/8` keeps following the script. Used by `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-05`.
- `stand-in-stopped`: nothing listens on the port that `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` names. Used by `SVC-API-CLIENT-11`, `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-03`, `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-04`, `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-05`, `E2E-DASHBOARD-03`.
- `desktop-viewport` is 1280 by 800 CSS pixels (default for UI items) and `phone-viewport` is 375 by 812 CSS pixels. Used by `UI-RESPONSIVE-LAYOUT-01`, `UI-RESPONSIVE-LAYOUT-02`, `UI-RESPONSIVE-LAYOUT-03`, `UI-RESPONSIVE-LAYOUT-04`, `UI-RESPONSIVE-LAYOUT-05`.
- `port-override`: the process environment sets `PORT=3100` for the development server. Used by `CLI-SCAFFOLD-02`.
- `secret-canary`: the process environment of the build contains `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-test-canary` and `DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://canary:canary-pass@localhost:5432/canary`. Used by `CLI-SCAFFOLD-06`.
- E2E items run with `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1` and the real API's default `CORS_ORIGINS`; the browser opens the frontend at `http://localhost:3000`.
- `TZ=UTC`

## Quality gates

Each gate must pass for the feature to be considered ready. Backend gates run from `backend/` and frontend gates run from `frontend/`.

- **Backend format** — `uv run ruff format .` — completes with exit code 0 and leaves the backend tree formatted
- **Backend lint** — `uv run ruff check .` — completes with exit code 0 and reports no violations
- **Backend tests** — `uv run pytest` — completes with exit code 0; every non-integration test passes
- **Frontend lint** — `npm run lint` — completes with exit code 0 and reports no ESLint errors
- **Frontend typecheck** — `npm run typecheck` — completes with exit code 0 and reports no TypeScript errors
- **Frontend tests** — `npm test` — completes with exit code 0; every unit and component test passes
- **Frontend enum duplication check** — `npm run check:enums` — completes with exit code 0 and finds no enum code or label literal in the application source
- **Frontend build** — `npm run build` — completes with exit code 0 and produces a production build

## Service

**Verification mode:** Invoke the public function or hook directly in-process (a hook through a minimal render harness, with a substitute for the browser event-stream class where the process has none), pointing the client at the stand-in API; assert the returned value, the rejected error, the hook state, or the record of requests the stand-in received. Consumers outside this feature: the bug pages (F11), the agent trace view (F12), the operations console (F13) and the search page (F14), which depend on F10 per PRD Section 8.

### API Client

**Common given:** the stand-in is running with the default scenario and its record of received requests is empty.

#### `SVC-API-CLIENT-01` — trailing slash in the base URL is normalized
- given: the `trailing-slash` configuration
- when: call the stats operation
- then:
  - the stand-in records exactly one request: GET `/api/v1/stats` with a single slash between the base and the path
  - the resolved value equals `stats-populated.json`

#### `SVC-API-CLIENT-02` — default base URL when the variable is unset
- given: the configuration with `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` unset, and the transport substituted by a recorder
- when: call the health operation
- then:
  - the recorded request URL is `http://localhost:8000/api/v1/health`

#### `SVC-API-CLIENT-03` — system reads return typed bodies
- given: (default)
- when: call the health, enums and stats operations in turn
- then:
  - the stand-in records GET `/api/v1/health`, GET `/api/v1/meta/enums` and GET `/api/v1/stats` in that order
  - the enums operation resolves to the contents of `enums.json`
  - the stats operation resolves to the contents of `stats-populated.json`

#### `SVC-API-CLIENT-04` — bug reads use the F09 paths and query names
- given: (default)
- when: call the bug list operation with status `open`, component `backend`, page 2 and page size 20, then the bug detail, similar bugs, bug runs and JSON report operations for bug 1
- then:
  - the list request carries query parameters `status=open`, `component=backend`, `page=2` and `page_size=20` and no others
  - the stand-in records GET `/api/v1/bugs/1`, GET `/api/v1/bugs/1/similar`, GET `/api/v1/bugs/1/runs` and GET `/api/v1/bugs/1/report`
  - the report request carries `format=json`

#### `SVC-API-CLIENT-05` — search and run reads use the F09 paths
- given: (default)
- when: call the search operation with text "login token" and limit 10, then the recent runs operation with limit 10 and type `triage`, then the run detail operation for run 7
- then:
  - the search request carries `q=login%20token` (or the plus-encoded equivalent) and `limit=10`
  - the recent runs request carries `limit=10` and `type=triage` and resolves to at most 10 items of `runs-recent.json` in the order served
  - the run detail request is GET `/api/v1/runs/7` and resolves to `{run, steps, logs}`

#### `SVC-API-CLIENT-06` — bug writes send JSON bodies
- given: (default)
- when: call the create bug, edit bug and reopen operations
- then:
  - create sends POST `/api/v1/bugs` with header `Content-Type: application/json` and the bug fields as the body
  - edit sends PATCH `/api/v1/bugs/{id}` with only the changed fields
  - reopen sends POST `/api/v1/bugs/{id}/reopen` with the body `{"confirm": true}`

#### `SVC-API-CLIENT-07` — operations and triage writes resolve run ids
- given: (default)
- when: call the init, seed, reset, index, triage-one and triage-all operations
- then:
  - the stand-in records POST `/api/v1/admin/db/init`, `/api/v1/admin/db/seed`, `/api/v1/admin/db/reset`, `/api/v1/admin/index` and `/api/v1/triage-runs` (twice)
  - reset sends the body `{"confirm": true}`
  - triage-one sends `{"bug_id": <id>}` and triage-all sends `{"all": true}`
  - seed, index and triage resolve to an object with a `run_ids` list

#### `SVC-API-CLIENT-08` — report text formats resolve to text
- given: (default)
- when: call the report operation with format `md`, then with format `html`
- then:
  - each request carries the matching `format` query parameter
  - the resolved values are strings, not parsed JSON

#### `SVC-API-CLIENT-09` — API error envelope becomes a typed error
- given: (default), and the stand-in answers GET `/api/v1/bugs/999999` with status 404 and the envelope code `not_found`
- when: call the bug detail operation for bug 999999
- then:
  - the call rejects with an error carrying status 404, code `not_found` and the envelope message
  - the error exposes the envelope `details` list

#### `SVC-API-CLIENT-10` — per-field validation details are preserved
- given: the `validation-error` configuration
- when: call the create bug operation
- then:
  - the call rejects with an error carrying status 422 and code `validation_error`
  - the error `details` equal the envelope details, field by field

#### `SVC-API-CLIENT-11` — unreachable API becomes a network error
- given: the `stand-in-stopped` configuration
- when: call the stats operation
- then:
  - the call rejects with an error carrying status 0 and code `network_error`
  - the error message names the configured base URL and says the API cannot be reached
  - the error message contains no stack trace

#### `SVC-API-CLIENT-12` — a non-envelope error body becomes a generic HTTP error
- given: the `bad-gateway` configuration
- when: call the stats operation
- then:
  - the call rejects with an error carrying status 502 and code `http_error`
  - the error message is a fixed generic message, not the raw body

#### `SVC-API-CLIENT-13` — absent filters are omitted from the query
- given: (default)
- when: call the bug list operation with only the search text "a&b=c" and every other filter undefined
- then:
  - the request carries exactly one query parameter, `search`, whose decoded value is "a&b=c"

### Enum Provider

**Common given:** the stand-in is running with the default scenario; the provider has not loaded yet.

#### `SVC-ENUM-PROVIDER-01` — one request serves every consumer
- given: (default), and two independent consumers use the provider
- when: the provider loads
- then:
  - the stand-in records exactly one GET `/api/v1/meta/enums`
  - the provider status becomes `ready`
  - both consumers see the same enums

#### `SVC-ENUM-PROVIDER-02` — label and value lookups come from the API response
- given: (default), and the provider is ready
- when: look up the label of `BugStatus` code `processed` and the values of `Severity`
- then:
  - the label equals the label in `enums.json` for that code
  - the values are returned in the order served, each with code, label and definition

#### `SVC-ENUM-PROVIDER-03` — unknown codes fall back to the code
- given: (default), and the provider is ready
- when: look up the label of `Component` code `quantum` and of an enum named `Nope`
- then:
  - both lookups return the code they were given
  - no request is sent to the stand-in

#### `SVC-ENUM-PROVIDER-04` — load failure is reported and retry recovers
- given: the `enums-unavailable` scenario
- when: the provider loads, then the scenario is switched to `populated` and the provider retries
- then:
  - after the first load the status is `error` and the error carries the message "Database is unavailable"
  - during the error, a label lookup returns the code it was given (no invented label)
  - after the retry the status is `ready` and labels come from the response

### Run Progress

**Common given:** the stand-in is running with the default scenario, which serves run 7 as finished and run 8 as a live run; the hook is started with a run id.

#### `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-01` — a finished run streams its full history and closes
- given: (default), and the hook is started with run 7
- when: the stream delivers all events of run 7
- then:
  - the hook transport is `sse`
  - the state holds the five steps ordered by position, each exactly once
  - the state holds the four log lines and the run with status `succeeded`
  - the hook status becomes `done` and the stream is closed

#### `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-02` — live events update the state as they arrive
- given: (default), and the hook is started with run 8
- when: the stand-in emits the step 1 `running` event of its script
- then:
  - within 1,000 ms the state shows step 1 with status `running`
  - the hook status is `streaming`

#### `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-03` — polling replaces an unavailable stream
- given: the `no-sse` scenario, and the hook is started with run 8
- when: the stream request is answered with status 404
- then:
  - the hook transport becomes `polling`
  - the stand-in records GET `/api/v1/runs/8` at intervals of about 1,000 ms
  - the state follows the script, with steps ordered by position

#### `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-04` — polling stops at a terminal status
- given: the `no-sse` scenario, and the hook is polling run 8
- when: a poll response reports the run with status `succeeded`
- then:
  - the hook status becomes `done`
  - the stand-in records no further GET `/api/v1/runs/8` during the following 3,000 ms

#### `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-05` — an interrupted stream continues by polling without duplicates
- given: the `sse-drop` scenario, and the hook is started with run 8
- when: the stand-in closes the stream after two events
- then:
  - the hook transport becomes `polling`
  - the state holds each step at most once per position and each log line at most once
  - the hook status becomes `done` when the run reaches `succeeded`

#### `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-06` — stopping the hook cancels all network activity
- given: (default), and the hook is started with run 8 and has received its first event
- when: the consumer stops using the hook
- then:
  - the stream is closed
  - the stand-in records no further requests for run 8 during the following 3,000 ms

#### `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-07` — no run id means no activity
- given: (default)
- when: the hook is started with no run id
- then:
  - the hook status is `idle`
  - the stand-in records no request

#### `SVC-RUN-PROGRESS-08` — an unknown run ends in an error
- given: the `no-sse` scenario, and the hook is started with run 999999
- when: the poll request is answered with status 404 and the code `not_found`
- then:
  - the hook status becomes `error` and the error carries the code `not_found`
  - the stand-in records no further poll after the first 404

## CLI

**Verification mode:** Spawn the command from the `frontend/` directory with the given environment; assert stdout, stderr, exit code, the listening port and, where stated, the files it produces.

### Scaffold

#### `CLI-SCAFFOLD-01` — the development server listens on port 3000
- given: dependencies installed; nothing listens on port 3000; the default configuration
- when: run `npm run dev`
- then:
  - the process keeps running and its output names a local address with port 3000
  - GET `http://localhost:3000/` answers 200 with a `text/html` body

#### `CLI-SCAFFOLD-02` — the development server honours the port variable
- given: dependencies installed; the `port-override` configuration; nothing listens on ports 3000 and 3100
- when: run `npm run dev`
- then:
  - the process listens on port 3100
  - nothing listens on port 3000

#### `CLI-SCAFFOLD-03` — the lint command passes
- given: dependencies installed
- when: run `npm run lint`
- then:
  - the exit code is 0
  - the output reports no error

#### `CLI-SCAFFOLD-04` — the production build succeeds with the four routes
- given: dependencies installed
- when: run `npm run build`
- then:
  - the exit code is 0
  - the build output lists the routes `/`, `/bugs`, `/search` and `/operations`

#### `CLI-SCAFFOLD-05` — the framework version is pinned exactly
- given: dependencies installed
- when: read the `next` entry of `frontend/package.json` and the installed Next.js version
- then:
  - the `next` entry is a bare version with no range operator
  - the installed version equals that entry
  - `frontend/package-lock.json` exists

#### `CLI-SCAFFOLD-06` — no secret reaches the browser bundle
- given: the `secret-canary` configuration
- when: run `npm run build`
- then:
  - no file under `frontend/.next/static` contains the string `sk-test-canary`
  - no file under `frontend/.next/static` contains the string `canary-pass`
  - no file under `frontend/src` reads a process environment variable other than `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL`

### Enum Source Check

#### `CLI-ENUM-SOURCE-01` — the application source holds no enum literal
- given: dependencies installed; `frontend/tests/fixtures/enums.json` lists every enum code and label
- when: run `npm run check:enums`
- then:
  - the exit code is 0
  - the output states that no enum literal was found under `frontend/src`

#### `CLI-ENUM-SOURCE-02` — a planted enum literal is detected
- given: a copy of the project in which one file under `src` contains the string literal "Needs info"
- when: run `npm run check:enums` in the copy
- then:
  - the exit code is non-zero
  - the output names the offending file and the literal

## UI

**Verification mode:** Render the surface in a browser against the running development server, drive it with user-like inputs (clicks, keyboard), and assert observable surface state (DOM, accessibility roles and names, visible text, navigation, and the record of requests received by the stand-in).

### Navigation

**Common given:** the default configuration and the `desktop-viewport`.

#### `UI-NAVIGATION-01` — four primary links in order
- given: (default)
- when: open `http://localhost:3000/`
- then:

### Dashboard States

**Common given:** the `desktop-viewport`.

#### `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-01` — loading state while data is pending
- given: the `slow` scenario
- when: open `http://localhost:3000/`
- then:
  - a loading indicator with the accessible role `status` and the text "Loading" is visible before the replies arrive
  - no count and no error banner is visible before the replies arrive
  - after the replies arrive the loading indicator is gone and the counts are visible

#### `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-02` — empty database shows the empty state
- given: the `empty` scenario
- when: open `http://localhost:3000/`
- then:
  - the text "No bugs yet. Go to Operations to initialize and seed the database." is visible
  - the text offers a link "Operations" that leads to `/operations`
  - no count group is shown

#### `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-03` — API down shows an error banner with Retry
- given: the `stand-in-stopped` configuration
- when: open `http://localhost:3000/`
- then:
  - an error banner with the accessible role `alert` is visible and says the API cannot be reached
  - a button "Retry" is visible and enabled
  - no count group is shown

#### `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-04` — Retry recovers when the API returns
- given: the error banner of `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-03` is shown, and the stand-in is then started with the default scenario
- when: click the button "Retry"
- then:
  - the error banner disappears
  - the counts of `stats-populated.json` are shown

#### `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-05` — Retry while the API is still down keeps the banner
- given: the error banner of `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-03` is shown and the stand-in is still stopped
- when: click the button "Retry"
- then:
  - the error banner is visible again after the attempt
  - the button "Retry" is enabled again

#### `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-06` — an API error message is shown to the user
- given: the `unavailable` scenario
- when: open `http://localhost:3000/`
- then:
  - the error banner contains the text "Database is unavailable"
  - a button "Retry" is visible

#### `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-07` — missing enums are an error, not a fallback
- given: the `enums-unavailable` scenario
- when: open `http://localhost:3000/`
- then:
  - an error banner is visible with a button "Retry"
  - no count group with raw codes such as "open" or "processed" is shown

#### `UI-DASHBOARD-STATES-08` — a failing runs request shows the error banner
- given: the `runs-error` scenario
- when: open `http://localhost:3000/`
- then:
  - an error banner is visible containing the text "Internal server error"
  - a button "Retry" is visible

## E2E

**Verification mode:** Run the full system (frontend development server, real F09 API, Postgres); drive it through a real browser at the `desktop-viewport`; assert cross-stack behavior, comparing what the page shows with direct calls to the API.

### Dashboard

#### `E2E-DASHBOARD-01` — page values equal the API values
- given: `seeded-database` and the real API running
- when: open `http://localhost:3000/`, then GET `/api/v1/stats` and GET `/api/v1/runs?limit=10` directly from the API
- then:
  - the total and each status, component and severity count shown equal the values returned by `/stats`
  - the status group shows open 20 and 0 for every other status
  - the run ids listed equal the ids returned by `/runs`, in the same order
  - the seed run is listed with type label "Seed" and status label "Succeeded"

#### `E2E-DASHBOARD-02` — an empty database shows the empty state
- given: `empty-database` and the real API running
- when: open `http://localhost:3000/`
- then:
  - the text "No bugs yet. Go to Operations to initialize and seed the database." is visible
  - no error banner is visible

#### `E2E-DASHBOARD-03` — API outage and recovery
- given: `seeded-database`, the Dashboard is open showing total 20, and the real API is then stopped
- when: reload the page, then start the API again and click the button "Retry"
- then:
  - after the reload the error banner and the button "Retry" are visible
  - after "Retry" the error banner disappears
  - the total 20 is shown again

#### `E2E-DASHBOARD-04` — new data appears on the next load
- given: `empty-database`, the real API running, and the Dashboard open showing the empty state
- when: send POST `/api/v1/admin/db/seed` directly to the API, wait until the returned run has status `succeeded`, then reload the page
- then:
  - the total 20 and the status entry "Open" with 20 are shown
  - the run list contains the seed run

### Enum Labels

#### `E2E-ENUM-LABELS-01` — labels equal the API labels
- given: `seeded-database` and the real API running
- when: open `http://localhost:3000/`, then GET `/api/v1/meta/enums` directly from the API
- then:
  - each label shown in the status group equals the `BugStatus` label returned by the API for that code
  - each label shown in the component group equals the `Component` label returned by the API, including "UI/UX"
  - each label shown in the severity group equals the `Severity` label returned by the API
